[THOUGHT]  
The clinical presentation—prolonged fatigue, easy bruising, fever, bone pain (nocturnal leg pain), and pancytopenia with marked leukocytosis and thrombocytopenia—is highly concerning for acute leukemia in a young child. The CBC shows anemia (Hb 10.1 g/dL), extreme leukocytosis (63,000/mm³), and severe thrombocytopenia (27,000/mm³)—a classic triad suggestive of bone marrow infiltration. The absence of overt bleeding or pallor does not rule out malignancy; early or compensated presentations may lack these signs. The bone marrow aspirate showing predominance of immature cells positive for CD10, CD19, and TdT is diagnostic of **B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL)**—the most common childhood leukemia. CD10 (CALLA), CD19 (B-cell lineage marker), and TdT (terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase) are hallmark immunophenotypic markers of precursor B-cell ALL.

[SUMMARY]  
**Clinical Impression:**  
Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (B-precursor type), high suspicion based on:  
- Age: 4-year-old female  
- Symptoms: 3-week history of fatigue and easy bruising; 1-week progression with fever and severe nocturnal bone pain  
- Laboratory findings:  
  • Anemia (Hb 10.1 g/dL)  
  • Marked leukocytosis (WBC 63,000/mm³) with likely circulating blasts (inferred from marrow findings)  
  • Severe thrombocytopenia (Plt 27,000/mm³)  
- Bone marrow immunophenotype: CD10+, CD19+, TdT+ → consistent with **B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma**, NOS (per WHO classification)  

**Next Steps Recommended (not stated but clinically indicated):**  
- Urgent referral to pediatric hematology/oncology  
- Additional diagnostics:  
  • Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis for CNS involvement  
  • Cytogenetics (karyotype) and molecular studies (e.g., ETV6-RUNX1, hyperdiploidy, KMT2A rearrangements)  
  • Comprehensive metabolic panel, LDH, uric acid, coagulation studies (DIC screen)  
- Initiation of risk-stratified therapy per contemporary protocols (e.g., COG AALL1732 or BFM-based regimens) after confirmation and staging  

**Note:** Peripheral blood smear review was ordered but result not provided; however, the marrow immunophenotype is definitive for B-ALL in this context.

[THOUGHT]  
This is a classic presentation of pediatric B-precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL). The patient is a 4-year-old female — the peak age for B-ALL — with subacute systemic symptoms (fatigue, easy bruising) progressing to alarm features (fever, severe nocturnal bone pain), all highly suggestive of bone marrow infiltration and systemic inflammation. Laboratory findings show a triad of cytopenias (anemia, thrombocytopenia) plus marked leukocytosis — a pattern commonly seen in ALL, especially with high blast burden. Although peripheral blood smear is pending, the bone marrow immunophenotype is definitive: CD10+, CD19+, TdT+ is the hallmark immunophenotypic signature of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma, NOS, per WHO classification. These markers confirm lineage (B-cell), immaturity (TdT), and precursor stage (CD10+/CD19+). No conflicting markers (e.g., myeloid or T-lineage antigens) are mentioned, and there is no evidence supporting alternative diagnoses (e.g., AML, lymphoma, infection, or aplastic anemia). • Patient is a 4-year-old female — peak age for B-precursor ALL  
• 3-week history of fatigue and easy bruising — consistent with progressive bone marrow failure  
• 1-week progression with fever and severe nocturnal bone pain — classic for marrow expansion and cytokine release in ALL  
• Anemia (Hb 10.1 g/dL) — evidence of erythroid suppression  
• Marked leukocytosis (WBC 63,000/mm³) — often driven by circulating blasts in ALL  
• Severe thrombocytopenia (Plt 27,000/mm³) — evidence of megakaryocyte suppression  
• Bone marrow immunophenotype: CD10+, CD19+, TdT+ — diagnostic of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma, NOS per WHO  
• Clinical context excludes reactive causes (e.g., no reported chronic infection, autoimmunity, or drug exposure)  

[GAPS]  
• Peripheral blood smear result — pending; would confirm presence/morphology of blasts but is not required for diagnosis given definitive marrow immunophenotype  
• Cytogenetic and molecular studies (e.g., karyotype, ETV6-RUNX1, hyperdiploidy) — needed for risk stratification, not diagnosis

B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma, NOS (B-precursor type)
